Hi Jordan — Aditya here (runtime infra). Quick technical notes based on your numbers:

- Concurrency & throughput: 150 concurrent sessions with 1 request / 10s => ~15 QPS sustained with peaks higher. With continuous batching we can maintain cost efficiency; however, batching adds tail latency variability. For strict p95 <200ms we typically avoid large batch windows on the critical path and rely on dedicated pools pinned to a model variant.

- Token limits & latency: context window increases do not scale linearly. Moving from 8k to 32k increases transformer compute roughly 4x for full attention when using a naive implementation. Our optimized kernels and KV-caching reduce that for incremental generation, but initial request latency (for large inputs) will still increase substantially. For example, on our dedicated MLC-48 pool:
  • 8k input + 512 output: cold p95 ~ 180ms (with pinned warm caches)
  • 32k input + 512 output: cold p95 ~ 520ms — initial attention pass is the driver here

- Streaming: streaming reduces perceived latency for the user since tokens are flushed as generated. For strict SLOs, we recommend streaming-first UX with early token flushing and incremental scoring on the client. That lets you hit perceived <200ms for the first tokens even if end-to-end generation is longer.

- Quantization & model variants: 8-bit quantized variants cut memory and often improve concurrency headroom; recommend we test both fp16 and q8 variants in the benchmark.

I’ll include these as notes in the perf sheet and draft an initial Dedicated config based on your concurrency numbers.

— Aditya

Jordan / Priya — attached is an updated perf sheet and a short SLA draft (SLA excerpt attached: sla_draft_20260701.pdf). Highlights and recommendations:

- Immediate pilot: run benchmark against your sample prompt set (please upload to the Drive link). We'll test: fp16 baseline, q8 variant, and a 32k-friendly variant. Expect a 3–5x delta in memory/compute between 8k and 32k for full-attention phases; incremental generation uses KV-cache to amortize cost when you stream multiple short outputs per session.
- SLO recommendation: For interactive flows where perceived latency matters, target streaming-first UX and optimize for "time-to-first-token" p95 < 200ms on Dedicated pinned pool. End-to-end generation p95 for long outputs (2k tokens) will likely be ~700–1200ms depending on model and quantization.
- Autoscaling: we'll propose a Dedicated pool sized for your 150 concurrent peak with headroom; if you want hosted first, we can run a short A/B to measure probability of meeting p95 targets under your burst profile.
